Thanks — captured some technical constraints and recommendations below. I focused on practical operator steps so Stellar can validate against their procurement/security expectations.

Summary recommendations:
- Root-of-trust: Keep the tenant master key inside customer HSM (BYOK). Redwood will only hold short-lived envelope keys encrypted to that master key (we never persist the unwrapped master).
- Onboarding modes:
  * Import (PKCS#11 wrapped key import): Customer provides wrapped KMS key material that we import into a software-protected vault for test/dev. For production, import directly into customer HSM or into a Cloud HSM under customer account if they permit.
  * Orchestrated wrap flow: We generate an envelope key and use an exportable wrapping key that the customer signs/unwraps on their HSM to accept the envelope key. This minimizes transfer of raw key material.
- Interface options: Support PKCS#11 for on-prem HSMs and Cloud HSM SDKs (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) for VPC peering. Redwood will provide a connector image that runs in customer VPC with a narrow egress to the HSM control plane.
- Envelope design: Use AES-GCM for data keys; envelope keys rotate independently (recommended cadence: 90 days for data keys, 12–18 months for wrapping/master keys depending on regen policy and compliance). Maintain key metadata including algorithm, created_by, rotation_count, previous_key_id references.
- Rotation and emergency rekey:
  * Planned rotation: schedule > testing > roll > validate. Keep old keys for read-only decryption window (7–30 days) depending on retention policy.
  * Emergency revoke: provide a signed revocation statement and a rewrap process; if master key is compromised, customer must rotate in their HSM and issue new wrap to Redwood connector. We will then rewrap all envelope keys under the new master and perform a phased rollout.
- Secrets handling: use a local vault (sealed/unsealed by HSM) for runtime secrets; no plaintext keys persist on disk. Use ephemeral in-memory key slots for active inference workloads and strict OS-level access controls.
- Audit/logging: Emit key operation events (unwrap/wrap/rotate) to both local syslog and to a read-only audit endpoint the customer controls. Timestamps must be canonical (UTC) and include request_id and operator_id.
- Network segregation: HSM traffic must traverse a customer-controlled subnet with ACLs. Management plane calls should be restricted to dedicated mgmt instances; data plane requests never touch the HSM directly (only wrapping/unwrapping ops).

Open questions for Stellar:
- Do you prefer an import-only model (HSM holds the master key) or an orchestrated wrap acceptance flow?
- Your acceptable window for keeping previous keys available after rotation? (regulatory minimums?)

I'll expand these into runbook steps and a rollback checklist for the next draft.

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our compliance team:

- We prefer import into our HSM (customer holds master) but need the wrap/orchestrated flow as a fallback for certain cloud regions. Can you document both flows end-to-end?
- Emergency rekey: acceptable read-only window after a master key rewrap is 14 days; can you confirm Redwood can support 14-day read-only after rotation?
- Audit delivery: we require daily batched exports of key usage logs to our S3 (encrypted) bucket plus streaming to our SIEM for critical events.

If you can surface the runbook with these two flows and confirm the 14-day window, we'll proceed with procurement and legal review.

—Asha
Asha Rao
Head of InfoSec, Stellar Payments

Asha / team — summary and owners below. Thanks for the clear feedback; we've updated the internal design doc (link below) and attached a revised runbook.

Decisions made:
- Primary model: import master into customer HSM (Stellar) — Redwood will operate envelope keys and never persist unwrapped master keys.
- Fallback: orchestrated wrap flow supported for regions where direct import is blocked.
- Read-only window: Redwood confirms support for a 14-day read-only decryption window after master rewrap.
- Audit delivery: we'll produce daily batched logs to Stellar S3 + real-time alerts for critical key events.

Action items:
- Dev: produce the detailed step-by-step runbook for both import and wrap flows, including test checklist (owner: dev.patel, due: 2026-03-26)
- Markus: finalize SLO amendment and send DocuSign (owner: markus.klein, due: 2026-03-27)
